items.authors: Yuxuan Hu, Jihao Liu, Weikang Shi et al.

items.title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather
items.summary: Urban traffic flow prediction is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, yet accurate forecasting under adverse weather conditions remains a significant challenge. Existing data-driven mo
items.authors: Zhu Xiao, Kuan Feng, Tong Li et al.

items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typic
items.authors: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao et al.

items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate
items.authors: Zheng Jiang, Fang Niu, Bo Peng et al.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.summary: This method caches LLM reasoning steps into CPU-executable code, allowing you to solve repetitive tasks much faster and cheaper without needing to re-run expensive model inference.
items.authors: Peter Belcak, Greg Heinrich, Saurav Muralidharan et al.

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.summary: The authors propose a new alignment technique that preserves both the overall data structure and specific pair-wise relationships, improving performance in complex multimodal machine learning tasks.
items.authors: Ruizhi Yuan, Zeqiu Yu, Wei Gao et al.

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: This paper demonstrates an AI-driven approach to discovering and verifying new quantum algorithms, potentially accelerating the development of quantum software beyond human-expert capabilities.
items.authors: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova et al.

items.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
items.summary: By using diffusion models to map protein language model activations, researchers can better interpret and steer complex protein representations without making rigid structural assumptions.
items.authors: Daniel Hinjos, Lucía Urcelay

items.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
items.summary: This research uses transformers to map muscle signals to robotic force, helping therapists create more effective, personalized rehabilitation plans that target actual neuromotor recovery.
items.authors: Gabriel Parra, Kimia Khoshnami, Daniel S. Brown et al.

items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.summary: The authors propose that dense user embeddings are actually combinations of interpretable behavioral patterns, offering a way to make opaque recommendation models more transparent and explainable.
items.authors: Jonathan Kozaczuk, Zheng Dong, Noyan Evirgen et al.

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: SwarmEvolve speeds up evolutionary search by using low-cost agents that process information in latent space, bypassing slow text generation to improve computational problem-solving efficiency.
items.authors: Qile Jiang, George Em Karniadakis

items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.summary: ReproBridge introduces a standardized framework for packaging ML research artifacts, helping agents and researchers more reliably reproduce experiments by capturing essential procedural context.
items.authors: Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Jaehyun Nam et al.

items.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment
items.summary: This framework evaluates conversational summaries by checking if the summary is logically supported by the source transcript, helping data scientists detect information loss from speech-to-text errors.
items.authors: Man-Ling Sung, Hemanth Kandula, Jeff Ma et al.

items.title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
items.summary: The authors propose using LLM-generated summaries of execution traces to more accurately benchmark agent performance, allowing for better evaluation with fewer task executions.
items.authors: Ben Johnson, Hayden Helm

items.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
items.summary: This research investigates how providing richer context to social simulation agents can reduce behavioral inconsistency, helping practitioners build more stable and reliable LLM-based social models.
items.authors: Mattia Greiche, Reihaneh Rabbany, Maximilian Puelma Touzel

items.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
items.summary: The authors demonstrate that generating multiple candidate actions at each step and using a selector model to pick the best one improves LLM agent performance on complex tasks.
items.authors: Jalaj Bhandari, Dhawal Gupta, Hongli Zhan et al.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.summary: The authors show that speculative decoding can introduce reasoning errors in long-horizon AI agents, suggesting that speed optimizations must be carefully validated for complex task planning.
items.authors: Hongyin Luo, Wei Fang, Lijie Yang et al.

items.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
items.summary: This framework uses LLM agents to automatically generate synthetic robot training data, significantly reducing the time and cost associated with manual teleoperation for robotics.
items.authors: Kewei Zhang, Juncheng Ma, Guodong Lv et al.

items.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.summary: The researchers propose treating recommendation systems as a two-way communication process between users and items, improving performance by giving items the same self-descriptive capabilities as users.
items.authors: Zhen Tao, Xun Zhou, Xuhui Chen et al.

items.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
items.summary: This compact neural network architecture accelerates gravitational-wave signal analysis by using spectral refinement, offering a faster alternative to traditional, computationally expensive SNR calculations.
items.authors: Ioannis Tsioulis, Anastasios Tefas, Nikolaos Stergioulas

items.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
items.summary: This benchmark helps developers detect when coding agents successfully complete tasks while simultaneously causing unintended system damage, preventing dangerous side effects from going unnoticed.
items.authors: Wei-Lin Chen, Zhepei Wei, Xinyu Zhu et al.

items.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
items.summary: WebHarbor provides a collection of stable, dockerized website environments, allowing researchers to train and test GUI agents on realistic, deterministic web workflows without relying on volatile live sites.
items.authors: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou et al.

items.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
items.summary: Researchers found that while Muon speeds up pretraining, AdamW remains the superior optimizer for fine-tuning large models trained on extensive datasets, providing better downstream performance.
items.authors: Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski et al.

items.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
items.summary: Strategist automates the creation of AI reasoning workflows by evolving and reusing code-based blueprints, moving away from manual, task-specific agent strategy design.
items.authors: Taiming Lu, Qi Xu, Zhigang Hua et al.

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: The authors propose a method to align language-based reasoning with continuous image generation, allowing multimodal models to achieve better controllability and scaling similar to large language models.
items.authors: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al.

items.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark that evaluates LLM negotiation skills by measuring the real-world economic impact of their agreements rather than just the dialogue quality.
items.authors: Xiangyu Kong, Ruirui Yang, Xia Hou

items.title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
items.summary: The researchers developed an automated system that continuously updates meta-analyses on human-AI collaboration, helping practitioners stay current with evolving evidence on effective AI integration.
items.authors: Michelle Vaccaro, Abdullah Almaatouq, Thomas W. Malone

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: The authors present a hierarchical world model that improves long-horizon planning for embodied agents by separating high-level state transitions from low-level control, reducing cumulative errors.
items.authors: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al.

items.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
items.summary: The researchers improve LLM safety by forcing models to make explicit, early safety decisions, helping practitioners better defend against multi-turn jailbreak attempts.
items.authors: Qiyao Ma, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang et al.

items.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
items.summary: This method embeds invisible watermarks into LLM text without slowing down inference or degrading output quality, offering a robust way to verify AI-generated content.
items.authors: Tom Sander, Pierre Fernandez, Itai Gat et al.

items.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
items.summary: A multi-agent framework uses LLMs to autonomously run scientific experiments and cross-verify findings, providing a blueprint for more reliable automated research workflows.
items.authors: El Mustapha Mansouri, Eikichi Kimura, Masato Koga et al.

items.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
items.summary: The authors propose a fine-tuning technique that dynamically adjusts teacher signals for every single token, leading to more precise and effective model distillation.
items.authors: Yifu Luo, Chuang Ma, Zeyu Chen et al.

items.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
items.summary: This method identifies specific fine-tuning data that inadvertently degrades model safety, helping developers audit training sets that bypass standard content filters.
items.authors: Saket Reddy, Amro Abbas, Anshuman Suri et al.

items.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
items.summary: PerceptRL improves multimodal model performance by using reinforcement learning to fix visual perception errors that standard caption-based training often overlooks.
items.authors: Tongkun Guan, Zhibo Yang, Mingkun Yang et al.

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: This framework filters out noisy or irrelevant agent failures before prompt optimization, ensuring that self-improving agents only learn from high-quality, actionable feedback.
items.authors: Zack Yu, Nicholas Lee, Minjae Lee et al.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: Researchers tested whether LLMs can autonomously discover unknown physical laws in simulated environments, providing insights into their capacity for independent scientific reasoning.
items.authors: Zhen Yang, Wen Wang, Xander Xu et al.

items.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
items.summary: The researchers developed a faster way for LLM agents to detect software vulnerabilities in real-time by reducing the compute-heavy reasoning steps required for security analysis.
items.authors: Amine Lbath, Massih-Reza Amini

items.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: EvoRouter optimizes multi-agent system configurations by using distillation to balance performance and cost, helping practitioners deploy complex agent workflows more efficiently.
items.authors: Yitao Xiao, Xu Zhang, Ye Cheng et al.

items.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
items.summary: DecisionRAG replaces traditional embedding-based retrieval with a decision model that evaluates document relevance directly, improving accuracy by avoiding the limitations of lexical matching.
items.authors: Chao Wan, Paul Jünger, Beixi Du et al.

items.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
items.summary: This paper introduces techniques for adding new languages to speech-to-text models without losing performance on previously learned languages, solving the problem of catastrophic forgetting.
items.authors: Yuchen Zhang, Haralambos Mouratidis, Ravi Shekhar

items.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
items.summary: The authors developed a compact, high-performance Persian retrieval model that outperforms existing small-scale alternatives, providing a practical tool for building efficient search systems in the Persian language.
items.authors: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Armon Rasooli

items.title: J-Comm: Jacobian-Guided Latent Communication between LLM Agents
items.summary: This framework improves collaboration between AI agents by allowing them to share latent reasoning states through geometric consensus and Jacobian-based interfaces, enhancing multi-agent problem solving.
items.authors: Xiangwei Wang, Wei Wang, Sachith Seneviratne et al.

items.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
items.summary: This study mathematically analyzes how embedding geometry and vocabulary size influence the learning performance of linear token predictors, offering insights into the fundamental generalization limits of language models.
items.authors: Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri, Flavio Nicoletti et al.

items.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
items.summary: The researchers propose a distillation method that transfers predictive knowledge from sequential recommenders to semantic-ID generative models, improving recommendation accuracy by leveraging item-level distributional data.
items.authors: Yixuan Xu, Hailin Liu, Linxiang Peng et al.

items.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
items.summary: The authors propose a framework for deciding when to trust an AI's output or escalate to a human auditor, helping practitioners minimize errors in high-stakes automated decision systems.
items.authors: Isaac Gibbs, Elise L. Han, Ryan J. Tibshirani et al.

items.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
items.summary: This paper demonstrates a cost-sensitive approach to AI classification that decides when an LLM should abstain from answering to avoid expensive errors, improving real-world operational efficiency.
items.authors: Sachin Gupta

items.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
items.summary: The researchers show that n-gram embedding tables in language models can be compressed using lower bit-precision to significantly reduce memory requirements without sacrificing performance.
items.authors: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du

items.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
items.summary: This study empirically investigates whether reinforcement learning training induces power-seeking behaviors in language models, providing crucial insights for developers concerned about long-term AI safety.
items.authors: Barış Alparslan, Sandy Tanwisuth, Caleb Petterson

items.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
items.summary: This method improves personalized federated learning by grouping clients based on their classifier heads, allowing for more effective model sharing without needing complex extra training steps.
items.authors: Amirardalan Dehghanpour, Arian Noori, Ehsan Tanghatari et al.

items.title: The End of Consensus Research?
items.summary: Researchers used AI to discover a new consensus protocol that significantly reduces latency in distributed systems, challenging the traditional reliance on purely human-designed algorithms.
items.authors: Clément Burgelin, Rachid Guerraoui, Zicong Hong et al.

items.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
items.summary: Quant-Arena provides a new benchmark to evaluate how well LLMs can autonomously perform the full quantitative trading research cycle, from hypothesis generation to strategy testing.
items.authors: Houde Qian, Zheng Jiang, Wenyi Li et al.

items.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
items.summary: ASTEROID uses a student-teacher framework to teach agents how to perform in-context exploration, overcoming the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning and imitation learning in partially observable environments.
items.authors: Sriyash Poddar, Yanda Bao, Jacob Krantz et al.

items.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
items.summary: This system enables warehouse robot fleets to share a memory of past events without overloading servers by only processing visual data when specifically requested.
items.authors: Jad Yammine, Malek Wahidi, Abrar Anwar et al.

items.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: The authors identify that agent training fails not just because of student errors, but because teachers often provide poor guidance in unfamiliar states, requiring better teacher-student alignment.
items.authors: Shu Zhao, Tan Yu

items.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
items.summary: This work introduces techniques to manage LLM memory usage by optimizing how key-value caches are stored and updated, preventing performance degradation during long task sequences.
items.authors: Tianyu Fu, Ruoxi Wang, Zihan Min et al.

items.title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
items.summary: This study evaluates when using LLMs for feature selection outperforms traditional statistical methods, providing guidance on when semantic context actually adds value to tabular data tasks.
items.authors: Fateme Memar, Dongjie Wang, Arvin Agah

items.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
items.summary: This framework improves multimodal agents by integrating external tools and memory, helping them solve complex visual tasks that base models cannot handle through reasoning alone.
items.authors: Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun et al.

items.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
items.summary: This method prevents catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon agents by dynamically switching between specialized LoRA adapters during task execution instead of using static model weights.
items.authors: Rui Shi, Xunjian Yin, Jiacheng Sang et al.

items.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
items.summary: This framework improves multi-robot navigation safety by allowing robots to share uncertainty estimates, enabling better coordination in unpredictable human-shared environments.
items.authors: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang et al.

items.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
items.summary: This study establishes a systematic way to measure how well language models improve their physical manipulation skills through self-correction, identifying key bottlenecks in their learning process.
items.authors: Zekai Li, Jiayi Yu, Jinlu Zhang et al.
